title: Guide: Send Crypto — Full Production Flow
description: End-to-end tutorial for sending on-chain crypto in production: gas estimation, idempotency key pattern, status polling, and webhook handling.
content: This guide covers the complete production flow for sending crypto with Yativo. Step 1: Estimate gas — call POST /transactions/get-gas-price with chainType, priority ('low', 'medium', or 'high'), and amount_usd. Use the estimated_gas_fee_usd to show the user the total cost before confirmation. Step 2: Send with idempotency — call POST /transactions/send-funds with account (account_id), assets (asset_id), receiving_address, amount, type ('crypto'), chain, category ('transfer'), priority, and a unique Idempotency-Key header (use a UUID like crypto.randomUUID()). If your network request times out without a response, retry with the same idempotency key — you will get either the original response or a 409 conflict with existing_transaction_id. Step 3: Poll for status — call POST /transactions/get-transactions with a search filter for the transaction_id, or use GET /unified-transactions/{id}. Status progresses: submitted → confirmed → completed. Step 4: Handle webhooks — listen for transaction.{type}.completed events on your registered webhook endpoint. Verify the X-Yativo-Signature header before processing (HMAC-SHA256 of timestamp.body). Common errors table: insufficient_balance (check balance first), invalid_address (validate address format before sending), gas_station_empty (top up gas station), rate_limit_exceeded (implement exponential backoff).

title: Guide: Accept Crypto Payments via Payment Gateway
description: Full tutorial for integrating the crypto payment gateway: authenticate, apply, create a payment link, share with customer, receive webhook, fulfill order.
content: This guide walks through integrating the Yativo crypto payment gateway for accepting payments. Step 1: Authenticate — POST /auth/token with api_key and api_secret. Step 2: Apply for gateway — POST /crypto-gateway/apply with logo_url, support_email, social_media_url, business_type, expected_volume, website_url, and webhook_url. Wait for approval (status: pending_review → approved). Step 3: Create a payment — POST /crypto-gateway/payments with title (what you are charging for), requested_amount (USD), accepted_assets (array of {chain, ticker} tokens you accept e.g. [{chain: 'solana', ticker: 'USDC'}]), customer_email, and external_reference (your internal order ID). Step 4: Share checkout_url — redirect the customer or embed the checkout_url in your UI. The hosted page shows your logo, amount, and accepted tokens with a QR code. Step 5: Poll or wait for webhook — either poll GET /crypto-gateway/pay/{id}/status (no auth required — safe to call from browser) or listen for the gateway.payment.settled webhook event on your registered URL. Step 6: Fulfill order — on gateway.payment.settled, verify the external_reference matches your order and mark it complete. Handle underpayments by checking gateway.underpayment.reported and using the reconciliation endpoints (/reconciliation/{id}/verify, /reverse, /reconcile, /settle-as-paid) to decide the business resolution.

title: Guide: Set Up Agentic Wallet for AI Agents
description: Step-by-step tutorial for creating and activating an agentic wallet, generating a connector key, funding the wallet, and making the first agent payment.
content: This guide walks through creating an agentic wallet for an AI agent in five steps. Step 1: Create wallet — POST /agentic-wallets/create with name ('My AI Agent Wallet'). Response: wallet_id (aw_ prefix) and status: pending_activation. Step 2: Activate wallet — First request an OTP: POST /agentic-wallets/{wallet_id}/activation/send-email-otp (no body). Check your email for the OTP. Then activate: POST /agentic-wallets/{wallet_id}/activation/activate with { email_otp: '123456' }. Response: status: active and the wallet's on-chain address. Step 3: Add connector — POST /agentic-wallets/{wallet_id}/connectors with name, per_transaction_limit (USD max per transaction), daily_limit, and monthly_limit. Response: connector_id and api_key (yac_ prefix) — store the api_key securely, shown only once. Step 4: Fund wallet — either send USDC to the wallet's on-chain address, or call POST /agentic-wallets/{wallet_id}/fund with { amount: 100 }. Step 5: Make payment — using the yac_ connector key as a Bearer token, call POST /agent/transact with wallet_id, amount, recipient_address, service_name ('OpenAI'), payment_reason ('GPT-4 inference'). For MCP-based AI clients (Claude Desktop, etc.): install @yativo/mcp-server globally, then configure mcpServers with YATIVO_API_KEY set to the yac_ key and YATIVO_WALLET_ID set to the wallet_id. The agent can then send payments by natural language instruction.

title: Guide: Swap Tokens (Cross-Chain and Same-Chain)
description: Complete tutorial for token swaps: browse assets, find routes, get quote, execute, and monitor status. Covers quote expiry handling and fee breakdown.
content: The complete token swap flow in Yativo Crypto covers five steps. Step 1: Browse swap assets — GET /swap/assets returns all swappable tokens with assetId, symbol, chain, canSwapFrom, canSwapTo flags. Filter canSwapFrom: true for source options. Step 2: Find routes — GET /swap/routes?fromAsset={assetId}&toAsset={assetId} returns available routes between the pair: routeId, protocol (bridge-standard, bridge-fast), estimatedTimeSeconds, estimatedFeeUsd, and tags (cross-chain, fast). Pick based on speed vs cost preference. Step 3: Get quote — POST /swap/quote with from_chain, from_ticker, to_chain, to_ticker, amount, from_address, to_address (and optionally routeId). Returns quoteId, toAmount (after fees), exchangeRate, fees (protocolFee, networkFee, yativoFee, totalFeeUsd), and expiresAt. Quotes expire in ~3 minutes. Build a 30-second buffer: if expiresAt is within 30 seconds, request a fresh quote before executing. Step 4: Execute — POST /swap/execute with quoteId, accountId, and Idempotency-Key header. Response: swapId and status: pending. Step 5: Monitor — GET /swap/history?swapId={id} for status updates. Statuses: pending, in_progress, completed, failed, refunded. Completed response includes actualToAmount which may differ slightly from quote due to slippage. Fee breakdown: protocolFee (DEX/bridge fee), networkFee (gas on source and destination chains), yativoFee (platform fee, 0% on most routes). Cross-chain swaps (e.g. USDC Ethereum to USDC Polygon) take 1-3 minutes via bridges.

title: Guide: Regional Payouts — Country-by-Country
description: Country-specific guide covering exact account_details fields for each payout rail: SPEI/Mexico, PIX/Brazil, NUBAN/Nigeria, ACH/USA, SEPA/Europe, Chile, Colombia, Peru, Argentina.
content: Every payout corridor has specific required fields for the account_details object in POST /beneficiaries/payment-methods. The general flow for all regions: GET /payment-methods/payout?country={iso3} to get payment_method_id → GET /beneficiary/form/show/{id} for exact required fields → POST /beneficiaries to create recipient → POST /beneficiaries/payment-methods with account_details → POST /sendmoney/quote → POST /sendmoney. Mexico SPEI: account_details requires clabe (18-digit CLABE). Validate check digit before submitting. Settlement same-day in minutes. For receiving MXN create virtual account with currency MXNBASE. Brazil PIX: account_details requires pix_key and pix_key_type (cpf, cnpj, phone, email, or evp). Settlement 24/7 under 10 seconds. For receiving BRL create virtual account with currency BRL (customers need brazil KYC endorsement). Nigeria NUBAN: account_details requires account_number (10-digit), bank_code (3-digit CBN code), account_name. Nigerian customers submitting KYC must include bvn (11 digits) and nin (11 digits). USA ACH: account_details requires account_number, routing_number (9-digit ABA), account_type (checking/savings), account_name. Settlement 1-3 business days. For receiving USD create virtual account with USDBASE. Europe SEPA: account_details requires iban (up to 34 chars), bic (SWIFT), account_name. SCT next business day, SCT Instant within 10 seconds. For receiving EUR use EURBASE or EURDE (Germany). Chile: account_number, bank_code, account_type, rut. Colombia: account_number, bank_code, account_type, document_type (CC/NIT/CE), document_number. Peru CCI: 20-digit account_number, bank_code. Argentina CBU/CVU: 22-digit cbu_cvu; virtual accounts with ARS require document_id and document_type (CUIT/CUIL/CDI). Always use GET /beneficiary/form/show/{payment_method_id} as the authoritative source for required fields — they may change as rails evolve.

title: Guide: Webhook Setup and Signature Verification
description: How to register webhooks, choose events, verify HMAC signatures, handle retries, and test delivery for both crypto and fiat APIs.
content: Setting up webhooks for both Yativo APIs. Crypto API: register with POST /webhook/create-webhook sending url and events array. Fiat API: register with POST /business/webhook sending url. Both return a webhook secret for signature verification. Crypto signature verification: headers include X-Yativo-Signature (sha256=hex_digest) and X-Yativo-Timestamp. Build the signed string: timestamp + '.' + JSON.stringify(payload). Compute HMAC-SHA256 using the secret. Compare with X-Yativo-Signature after stripping 'sha256='. Reject requests where timestamp is more than 5 minutes old (replay attack protection). Fiat signature verification: X-Yativo-Signature contains HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body (not JSON-stringified — use the raw bytes). Always use timing-safe comparison (e.g. crypto.timingSafeEqual in Node.js). Rotate secrets with POST /yativo-card/webhooks/{id}/rotate-secret (crypto). View delivery history with GET /yativo-card/webhooks/{id}/deliveries. Retry a failed delivery with POST /yativo-card/webhooks/deliveries/{id}/retry. Respond with HTTP 200 within 30 seconds to acknowledge. If your endpoint returns non-200 or times out, Yativo retries with exponential backoff. Idempotency tip: webhook events may be delivered more than once — make your event handlers idempotent by checking if the event was already processed before acting.

title: Guide: Issue Virtual Accounts and Receive Local Payments
description: Tutorial for issuing virtual accounts to customers, handling inbound payments, checking KYC requirements, and refunding deposits.
content: To receive local bank payments for your customers using virtual accounts: Step 1: Create a customer — POST /customer with customer_name, customer_email, customer_phone (E.164), customer_country (ISO 3-letter code), customer_type (individual or business). Step 2: Submit KYC — direct the customer through KYC verification. Check is_va_approved in GET /customer/{id}. This must be true before issuing virtual accounts. Step 3: Create virtual account — POST /business/virtual-account/create with customer_id and currency (BRL for PIX Brazil, MXNBASE for SPEI Mexico, USDBASE for ACH USA, EURBASE for SEPA Europe, ARS for Argentina with document_id and document_type). The response account_number is what your customer shares with senders. Step 4: Receive payments — when money arrives at that account number, the virtual_account.deposit webhook fires with the amount, sender info, and transaction_id. The virtual_account.funded webhook fires when the balance is updated. Step 5: Get transaction history — POST /business/virtual-account/history/{account_number} with optional date filters. Step 6: Manage accounts — suspend with PUT /business/virtual-account/enable_disable_virtual_account (action: disable). Resume with action: enable. Delete permanently with DELETE /business/virtual-account/delete-virtual-account/{id}. Refund a received payment with POST /business/virtual-account/refundPayin/{externalId} using the external transaction ID from the deposit webhook.

title: Guide: Auto-Forwarding Rules for Wallet Sweeping
description: Tutorial for creating auto-forwarding rules to automatically sweep wallet balances above a threshold to a treasury or cold wallet address.
content: Auto-forwarding lets you automatically move funds from hot wallets to a treasury address when balances exceed a threshold. Create a rule with POST /auto-forwarding. Required fields: asset_id (the asset to monitor — from POST /assets/add-asset), destination_address (treasury or cold wallet address), destination_chain (blockchain of the destination), min_amount (USD threshold to trigger forwarding — minimum $1 for same-wallet, minimum $10 for cross-wallet batching), enabled (boolean). Use case 1 — sweep collection wallets: each customer gets a collection wallet. When any wallet exceeds $100, auto-forward to your main treasury. Set min_amount: 100, enabled: true. Use case 2 — hot wallet security: maintain small operational balances by forwarding anything over $500 to cold storage. Use case 3 — cross-wallet batching: aggregate deposits from many small wallets into one when combined threshold exceeds $10. Manage existing rules: GET /auto-forwarding/{id} to view, PUT /auto-forwarding/{id} to update min_amount or toggle enabled, DELETE /auto-forwarding/{id} to remove. Trigger immediately without waiting for threshold: POST /auto-forwarding/forward. Each rule is per-asset — create separate rules for USDC on Ethereum vs USDC on Solana.

title: Guide: Compliance Address Screening
description: Tutorial for integrating address screening into your transaction flow to block sanctioned, fraud, and mixer addresses before sending or accepting crypto.
content: Integrate compliance screening into your transaction flow. The screener is a public API (no auth) at POST /screener/check with { address: '0x...' }. It returns risk_level (low, medium, high, critical), flagged (boolean), and checks (sanctions, fraud, darknet, mixer — each boolean). Recommended integration pattern for withdrawals: Before calling POST /transactions/send-funds, call POST /screener/check with the receiving_address. If risk_level is 'critical' or 'high', block the transaction and alert your compliance team. If risk_level is 'medium', queue for manual review. If flagged is false and risk_level is 'low', proceed. For deposits: when you receive a deposit.detected webhook, screen the sending address. Flag or hold the deposit if the address is high risk. Batch screening: POST /screener/batch-check to check multiple addresses at once — efficient for pre-screening address books or bulk operations. The screener checks: sanctions (OFAC, UN, EU, and other global sanctions lists), fraud (known fraud wallets and exchange theft), darknet (addresses linked to darknet markets), mixer (tornado cash, coinjoin, and other mixing services). Screen results are deterministic for the same address at the same time but may change as new intelligence is added.

title: Guide: Idempotency Key Patterns
description: Best practices for using Idempotency-Key headers to safely retry failed requests without duplicating transactions on both crypto and fiat APIs.
content: Idempotency keys prevent duplicate transactions when retrying failed or timed-out requests. Crypto API: Idempotency-Key is optional but strongly recommended on all write operations. Fiat API: Idempotency-Key is required on all POST/PUT/PATCH requests. Key generation: use a UUID per operation (crypto.randomUUID() in Node.js, uuid4() in Python). Alternatively compose keys from business context: 'send-{order_id}-{timestamp}' or 'payout-{userId}-{payrollDate}'. Key reuse rule: use the same key when retrying the exact same operation after a timeout or network error. Never reuse a key for a different operation or different parameters. On 409 Conflict (crypto API): the error body contains existing_transaction_id — use GET /unified-transactions/{id} or POST /transactions/get-transactions to retrieve the original and check its status rather than submitting a new transaction. On successful retry with same key: you receive the same response as the original successful request, not a duplicate transaction. Key expiry: idempotency keys are remembered for a finite period (typically 24 hours). Store the key alongside the transaction in your database so you can retrieve it for retries within that window. Fiat API pattern: generate a key before making the request, store it with the pending transaction record, then call the endpoint. If the call fails or times out, retry with the stored key.

title: Guide: Sandbox Testing
description: How to use the Yativo sandbox environments for testing without real funds. Crypto and fiat sandbox base URLs, test credentials, and simulating webhook events.
content: Yativo provides separate sandbox environments for development and testing. Crypto sandbox base URL: https://crypto-sandbox.yativo.com/api/v1. Fiat sandbox base URL: https://smtp.yativo.com/api/v1. Use sandbox-specific credentials (separate api_key/api_secret or account_id/app_secret from your sandbox account). Sandbox environments simulate the full API flow including transactions, webhooks, KYC flows, and card operations with test assets — no real funds are moved. Crypto sandbox: swap simulations run the full flow with test assets. Card operations simulate KYC approval and card transactions. Gas station works with test native tokens. Agentic wallet activation uses test email OTPs. Fiat sandbox: send-money flows simulate local rail settlement with test beneficiaries. Virtual account creation issues test account numbers that accept simulated deposits. KYC review is auto-approved in sandbox. All API responses from sandbox match production format exactly. Use the sandbox to test error handling: simulate insufficient_balance by sending more than the test wallet holds. Simulate quote expiry by waiting 5+ minutes before executing. Test webhook delivery by registering a webhook URL pointing to a tool like webhook.site or a local tunnel (ngrok).

title: Guide: Gas Station Setup and Management
description: How to set up the gas station to cover network fees for users, fund station assets, monitor balances, and handle gas_station_empty errors.
content: The gas station covers blockchain network fees on behalf of your users so they only need to hold the token they are sending — not a separate native token for gas. Setup steps: 1) Add a chain to the gas station — POST /assets/add-station-asset with chain and ticker (native gas token for that chain: ethereum/ETH, solana/SOL, polygon/POL, bsc/BNB, base/ETH_BASE, arbitrum/ETH_ARBITRUM, optimism/ETH_OPTIMISM, xdc/XDC). The response includes a station deposit address. 2) Fund the station — send native tokens from an external wallet to the station address. For example, send ETH to the Ethereum station address to cover gas for Ethereum transactions. 3) List station assets — POST /assets/get-station-assets to see all stations and their balances. Monitor with the gas.low webhook event which fires when reserves drop below a threshold. The 20% markup: Yativo charges 20% above actual network cost to cover gas — this is deducted from your gas station balance, not from the user's token. Alternative — use_self_funding: for native token transactions (sending ETH, SOL, BNB), set use_self_funding: true in POST /transactions/send-funds so the gas comes from the user's native token balance rather than the station. Error gas_station_empty (HTTP 422): top up the station address with native tokens. Recommended reserve: keep at least 0.1 ETH for Ethereum, 1 SOL for Solana, 10 MATIC for Polygon in each station.

title: Guide: B2B Card Issuer Program
description: Tutorial for platforms that want to issue virtual cards to their own customers: apply, set up master wallet, fund customers, and look up card holders.
content: The B2B card issuer program lets your platform issue branded virtual Visa/Mastercard cards to your own customers without requiring each customer to onboard directly with Yativo. Steps: 1) Apply — POST /card-issuer/apply with funding_structure ('master_wallet' to use a shared fund pool or 'non_master' for isolated wallets), optional iban_enabled. 2) Wait for approval — GET /card-issuer/status until approved. 3) Fund master wallet — GET /card-issuer/funding-addresses for the deposit addresses. Send USDC to fund your master wallet. View master wallets with GET /card-issuer/master-wallets. 4) Fund a customer's card — POST /card-issuer/fund-customer with customer identifier (customer_id, card_id, external_id, or email), amount, source_chain, pricing_mode ('send_x' to send a specific amount from master wallet, or 'receive_x' so the customer card receives a specific amount and fees are added on top). 5) Look up customers — GET /card-issuer/lookup-customer by identifier. List all customers with GET /card-issuer/customers. View funding history with GET /card-issuer/deposits. 6) Swap master wallet tokens — POST /card-issuer/master-wallets/swap with from_token, to_token, amount to rebalance between currencies in your master wallet. All customer card events (purchases, declines, freezes) fire webhooks to your registered endpoint.

title: Guide: Fiat KYC Flow — Individual and Business
description: End-to-end KYC flow for fiat customers: create customer, submit KYC documents to kyc.yativo.com, check approval status, handle endorsements and regeneration.
content: Complete KYC flow for fiat customers. Step 1: Create customer — POST /customer with name, email, phone (E.164), country (ISO 3-letter), type. Step 2: Submit KYC to the separate KYC service. For individual: POST https://kyc.yativo.com/api/individual-kyc/submit with personal info (name, DOB, nationality, gender), address (street, city, state, postal code, country), identification (document type, number, front/back image URLs), and risk_and_purpose (account purpose, expected volume, source of funds). Special requirement for Nigerian nationals: also include bvn (11-digit Bank Verification Number) and nin (11-digit National Identification Number). For businesses: POST https://kyc.yativo.com/api/business-kyc/submit with company info, registered address, beneficial owners, and business documents. Step 3: Check status — GET /customer/kyc/{customer_id} returns is_va_approved (boolean), endorsements array, and kyc_status. Step 4: Issue virtual account — only after is_va_approved: true. Some products need specific endorsements: PIX Brazil requires 'brazil', SEPA requires 'sepa', Germany SEPA requires 'eurde'. Step 5: Handle re-verification — if customer's docs expire or need update, use GET https://kyc.yativo.com/api/kyc/regenerate/{customer_id}/{service} to get a fresh KYC link for the relevant service. Webhook: customer.kyc.approved fires when approved, customer.kyc.rejected fires with rejection reason.
